title: Portugal's Growth Rebound Masks Deeper Tensions Over Inflation, Housing · 18 Aug
keywords: Portugal, GDP growth, inflation, housing, immigration, construction, labor shortage, European Union, cost of living, economic policy, Lisbon, Bank of Portugal, Eurostat
notes: Portugal posted stronger-than-expected GDP growth of 2.5% year-on-year in the second quarter, giving the government ammunition to argue the economy is proving resilient. Yet persistent inflation and a deepening construction labor shortage are undermining the official optimism, exposing a fault line between headline performance and daily household reality. The debate is not just domestic: it mirrors pressures felt across the European Union on migration, housing affordability, and the true cost of growth.
